messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bulgarian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bulgarian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Той изглеждаше, че идва срещу мен с висока глава и с яростен глад, така че изглеждаше, че въздухът трепери от него.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | Questi | demonstrative pronoun, the threatening opponent (subject) | Той | “he” | OK | | parea | verb “seemed”, speaker’s perception (predicate) | изглеждаше | “seemed” | OK | | che (1) | complementizer “that” introducing motion clause | че | “that” | OK | | contra | preposition “against” (direction) | срещу | “against” | OK | | me | 1st‑person pronoun, object of *contra* | мен | “me” | OK | | venisse | verb “to be coming” (imperfect subjunctive, motion) | идва | “comes / is coming” | OK | | con (1) | preposition “with” (first attribute) | с | “with” | OK | | la | definite article (feminine singular) – not required in Bulgarian | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | test' | noun “head” (body part) | глава | “head” | OK | | alta | adjective “high” (attribute of *test'*) | висока | “high” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | и | “and” | OK | | con (2) | preposition “with” (second attribute) | с | “with” | OK | | rabbiosa | adjective “ravening” (intense hunger) | яростен | “ravenous” | OK | | fame | noun “hunger” (object of *con*) | глад | “hunger” | OK | | sì | resultative adverb “so that” | така че | “so that” | OK | | che (2) | complementizer “that” introducing result clause | че | “that” | OK | | parea (2) | verb “seemed” (predicate of result clause) | изглеждаше | “seemed” | OK | | che (3) | complementizer “that” introducing inner clause | че | “that” | OK | | l'aere | noun “the air” (subject of trembling) | въздухът | “the air” | OK | | ne | clitic pronoun “of it / because of him” (causal) | от него | “from him / because of him” | OK | | tremesse | verb “trembled” (imperfect subjunctive) | трепери | “trembles” | OK |
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: *la* – the Italian definite article has no separate counterpart in Bulgarian; the definiteness is expressed by the suffix **‑ът** on *въздухът*.
All other source words are accounted for with appropriate Bulgarian equivalents and correct grammatical agreement.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bulgarian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bulgarian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
